🔸 الرايتنق :
أول وأهم خطوة سويتها صراحة كنت أركز على ستركتشر المس كانت تنزل السلايدات بالبلاك بورد فيها كل المتطلبات اللي هي تبغاها. وساعات كانت تكتب أشياء معينة بالبورد ف كنت أصورها عندي. بعد كذا كنت ألخص الستركتشر حقي بناءً على الأشياء اللي خذيتها مع المس في الكلاس. وفي نهاية التلخيص كنت أخلي مساحة فاضية أكتب فيها الفوكاب اللي أشوفه بيفيدني ( أبدأ أكتب اللي عندي من معرفتي السابقة وبعدين أشوف الفوكاب اللي يعجبني من السلايدات ). 
بعدها أبدأ أكتب رايتنق من المواضيع اللي موجودة في السلايدات ( وضروري أحط تايمر عشان أضبط وقتي ) هالخطوة مرة فادتني والحمدالله ما حسيت أني انزنقت ب ولا اختبار.

Dear Students,

Now that you have completed the midterm exam, I know many of you are anticipating the release of both your Writing Task 1 (WT1) grades and your midterm exam results in the coming days. Midterm exam results will be released on BlackBoard as Reading, Vocabulary, Grammar and Overall Letter Grade, in that order (e.g. A A A =A). WT1 results will be released as per the rubric (from Response to Question, to Language Use, plus an Overall summative letter grade; e.g. A A A A =A). Whenever grades are released, questions naturally follow. As you know, the English Language Department Policies and Procedures document was shared with you on Blackboard on the first day of the course, and you were asked to read it carefully. Some of the questions students raise at this stage are already addressed in that document. Nevertheless, this message clarifies two specific areas that I expect will generate the most questions: course/section averages and the type of feedback provided on assessments.

First, many students are curious about how they performed in relation to their peers and what the class average might be. I recently raised this question in a meeting, and I was informed that the policy remains that averages are not shared with students. The only information provided is that overall class performance for ENGL101 at the end of the semester is expected to fall within the C to C+ range. Beyond that, no further details about averages will be released. While it is natural to compare yourself with others, what is more productive is to consider whether you are satisfied with your own grade. If you are satisfied, then your current level of preparation is appropriate. If you are not satisfied, that is a clear indication that greater effort or adjustment is needed to be done by you outside of class before the next writing task or the final exam. Please understand that there will be no additional information provided regarding class averages.

Second, many students understandably request detailed, individual feedback on summative assessments. It is important to distinguish between formative and summative assessment. A formative assessment is designed to form and improve your understanding; it provides feedback intended to guide development before a final evaluation. In contrast, a summative assessment represents the sum of your performance at a specific point in time and results in a grade. As stated in the ELD Policies and Procedures (Section 1.2.9, p. 4), “Midterm and final exams are secure and, therefore, not shown to students. The practice essays are formative.  The exams are for summative assessment, not formative” . This distinction explains why detailed, individualized feedback is not provided for these assessments. However, for WT1 you do receive four separate letter grades corresponding to the rubric categories. These letters align with published descriptors. For example, if you received a D in Language Use, you can review the D-level box and identify the grammatical and vocabulary characteristics described there. Similarly, if you earned a B in Structure and Organization, you can compare your work against the B-level expectations. In this way, the WT1 rubric functions as a self-diagnostic tool. If you would like clarification about a specific descriptor, you are welcome to bring focused questions to office hours. Additionally, before future assessments, you will again have further opportunities for formative feedback. To strengthen grammar and vocabulary in particular, please review the materials available on Blackboard Ultra, including the links to our custom GPT tools, which are designed to provide targeted practice and feedback.

In conclusion, class averages and specific feedback will not be provided for the MTE or WT1. I strongly encourage you to consult the Policies and Procedures document if you have questions about assessment policies and procedures.

الرايتنق بيعطيك 3 prompts اختار/ي واحد منهم مثلًا :-

1- Saudi Arabia should ban Tiktok
2- KFUPM should allow VPN-free for students
3- KFUPM should allow all students in housing at campus
امثلة بس

المطلوب منك تكتبـ/ين 5 بارقرافات :
1- Introduction
2- Body Paragraph 1
3- Body Paragraph 2
4- Counter argument
5- Conclusion

1- Introduction
في هالبراقراف تقريبًا بيكون الوضع نفس اللي سويناه قبل Giving a background ممكن نجيب Recent situation فيه أكثر من طريقة نقدر نبدأ فيها موجودة في سلايدات cause and effect. بعد ما نخلص ونتكلم بشكل عام رح نذكر أهمية الموضوع وليش لازم نناقشه. آخر شيء الThesis حقتنا لازم يكون فيها
- The topic ( Must be rephrased ) يعني مُعادة صياغته
- The two reasons السببين اللي بتتكلم/ين عنهم في البودي
- The agent ( Already in the prompt )
مثال للthesis:
Psycological support and studying environment are two imperative reasons that in-campus housing should be permitted for all KFUPM students.
لاحظوا صياغتي مختلفة عن الprompt ف مهمة هالخطوة


2- Body Paragraph 1
في هذا البراقراف رح نبدأ نفصل السبب الأول حقنا ونشرح أكثر عنه ، ورح نبدأ بالTopic sentence ضرورية طبعًا وهنا ما يحتاج تسوون rephrase للتوبك ممكن تكتبونها زي ما هي بالانترو حقتكم بس اذا حبيتوا عادي
بعد كذا رح نبدأ الelaboration حقنا وعندنا أكثر من طريقة ونقدر نستخدم كل اللي تعلمناه بالتاسكات الاولى نقدر : Giving definitions (Explanation), Condition, Causes,Implecation,Comparasions هذه وغيرها طبعًا وتشرحون مع اهمية أنه كل مرتبط بالتوبك حقكم وبالthesis تحديدًا لا تطلعون برا الموضوع

3- Body Paragraph 2

SAME AS BP1🔺🔺

4- Counter argument
في هذا البارت احنا رح نوضّح وجهة النظر المختلفة عن رأينا ، بمعنى لو كنت مع الموضوع فأنا هنا رح أجيب العكس.
عندنا طريقتين للCounter argument:-
🔸Text-Based
🔸Imaginative

بالنسبة للاولى هذه رح تختارين واحد من أسبابك الاثنين وتوضحين وجهة النظر المعاكسة
مثلًا احنا كتبنا Psycological support as a purpose
بيقومون المعارضين يقولون طيب ممكن الطالب يتلقى الدعم من أهله والمحيط الخارجي
فهنا انت/ي اخترت/ي احد الاسباب ووضحتي كيف يفكر الشخص المعارض فيها

الثاني مختلف : رح تجيب/ن سبب خارجي ماهو موجود أبد باللي كتبتيه وهو بيكون رأي المعارضين
مثلًا : Limited budgets for students
هذا سبب خارجي ماله دخل أقصد أنه المكافأة محدودة فالطالب بيفضل المسافة البعيدة على أنه يدفع

نجي الحين للستركتشر حق هذا البارقراف
▫️ Sentence 1 : The opposite view ( Against and only one sentence )
▫️ Sentence 2 : Rebuttal : بمعنى رح ترجعين علطول لرأيك وتوضحين ليش هو الصحيح وكيف أنه السبب اللي كتبه الشخص المعارض خطأ
بالتالي ممكن تعطين اقتراحات ، حلول كيف نقدر نتخلص من هالسبب كونه يعتبر غير كافي لرفض الفكرة اللي هي موضوعنا
الRebuttal المفترض كحد أدنى 3 جمل

5- Conclusion
هنا تقريبًا نفس الفكرة رح نسوي اعادة صياغة للمرة الثانية للThesis حقتنا
بعدين رح نكتب Summary للبودي 1 و 2 واختياري للكاونتر بس مو اجباري
اخر شيء تختمين إما ب Strong statement, Recommendation, Or future possibility

وعليكم السلام والرحمة
بالنسبة للانترو المفترض انه محتوياتها كالتالي:
1- أولًا الفكرة العامة من موضوعك General Background تتكلم بشكل عام عن الموضوع وعندك أكثر من طريقة مختلفة تقدر تستخدمها بهالبارت مثلًا ممكن تجيب ظاهرة حديثة لها علاقة بالموضوع زي مثلًا مثلًا خلينا نقول موضوعنا عن التعليم عن بعد أو التعليم الحضوري فكّر فيها ايش ابرز حادثة صارت لها علاقة بالموضوع؟ كورونا صح فبتربط الموضوع بالحادثة هذه. ممكن تبدأ بdefinition يعني لو كان مثلًا عندك موضوع عن Saudization هذا قد كتبنا عنه ممكن نوضح هالمفهوم اللي يعني السعودة فهمت علي

2- بارت 2 هو الreason اللي انت تقصده. هذا البارت لازم توضح فيه ليش احنا قاعدين نتكلم عن الموضوع من الاساس، ليش قاعدين نقارن بين حاجتين أو ليش قاعدين نقنع القارئ بهالموضوع، اذكر اهمية الموضوع سواء هالوقت او بالمستقبل زي مثلًا نرجع لموضوع السعودة ممكن تذكر اهمية الاحتياج لتوظيف السعوديين وانه لازم نسلط الضوء على هالقضية من هالكلام يعني لازم تبيّن للقارئ أنه موضوعك له اهمية

3- البارت الاخير اللي هو اهم بارت بيكون الThesis statement وهذه من اسمها statement يعني جملة وحدة بتحتوي على : الموضوع نفسه، السببين أو المحورين اللي بتتكلم عنهم، وتوجهك عن الموضوع

Could have:
-when something was possible in the past, or you had the ability to do something in the past, but you didn't do it
-when something wasn't possible in the past, even if you had wanted to do it
-when making a guess about something that happened in the past (guessing
what maybe happened)

Should have:
-indicate a good idea that did not happen in the past (late advice)
-something you assume has already happened if everything is ok (used with “by now”)
-to talk about something that you expected to happen if everything was fine, but it
did not happened

Would have:
-you wanted to do something in the past but you were not able to (used with “but”)
-describes an action or activity that did not take place, but would definitely would have happened if the right condition had occurred first

The students, who were delayed by the accident, were given an extra time.

لو قلنا
The students were given an extra time

🟦 المقدمة (Introduction)

المقدمة لازم تكون من 3 إلى 4 جمل فقط، وتحتوي على:

1. جملة خلفية عامة: تعرّف بالموضوع أو المشكلة بشكل عام.


2. جملة توضح أهمية الموضوع: تشرح لماذا هذا الموضوع مهم للناس أو كيف يؤثر في حياتهم.


3. جملة مقارنة عامة: توضّح أن الخيارين متشابهين في الهدف لكن بينهم فروقات.


4. جملة الأطروحة (Thesis Statement): تذكر فيها النقطتين الرئيسيتين اللي راح تقارن بينهم (Focus Points).



> مثال: التكلفة – التواصل، أو المرونة – البيئة الاجتماعية.

🟨 الفقرة الأولى (Body Paragraph 1)

تركّز على أول نقطة مقارنة (Focus Point 1) وتشمل:

1. Topic Sentence: جملة تبدأ بها الفقرة وتوضح الفكرة الأساسية.


2. شرح ودعم: توضح كيف يختلف الخيار الأول عن الثاني في هذه النقطة.


3. أمثلة أو مواقف واقعية: مثال بسيط يوضّح الفرق.


4. جملة ختامية صغيرة: تربط الفكرة بالاختيار أو الغرض من المقارنة.



🔹 المطلوب: المقارنة الحقيقية بين الخيارين، مو مجرد ذكر المميزات فقط.

☆~...~...~...~....~...~...~....~....~....~....☆

🟩 الفقرة الثانية (Body Paragraph 2)

تتحدث عن ثاني نقطة مقارنة (Focus Point 2) وتشمل:

1. Topic Sentence جديدة: تبدأ بجملة انتقالية مثل ““Secondly …”.


2. شرح واضح: تشرح جانب القوة أو الضعف في كل خيار.


3. أمثلة أو تبريرات: توضح التأثير أو السبب وراء الفرق.


4. جملة ختامية تربط الفكرة بالاختيار.



🔹 المطلوب: توازن في المقارنة بين الجانبين، ما تميل لأحدهما فقط.

🟥 الخاتمة (Conclusion)

الخاتمة تتكوّن من 3 جمل فقط، وتشمل:

1. إعادة صياغة للأطروحة (Restated Thesis): تعيد الفكرة الأساسية بكلمات مختلفة.


2. ملخص سريع لأفكار الفقرتين: تذكّر القارئ بنقطتي المقارنة.


3. جملة توصية (Recommendation): توضح أي خيار يناسب نوعًا معينًا من الأشخاص، أو متى يكون كل خيار مفيدًا أكثر.



🔹 المطلوب: تكون الخاتمة بسيطة وواضحة، بدون أفكار جديدة أو أمثلة إضافية.

Text 5: The Problems of Wind and Solar Power

This essay argues that although wind and solar energy are promoted as solutions to climate change, they have serious limitations. The author focuses on low power density, meaning they require huge areas of land to generate useful amounts of energy. Another major issue is intermittency—energy is only produced when the sun shines or the wind blows—so fossil fuels are still needed as backup. Finally, the essay highlights the storage problem, explaining that electricity from wind and solar cannot be easily stored, making them unreliable and expensive for large-scale energy needs .

⸻

Text 6: Why Nuclear Is the Way Forward

This text presents nuclear power as the most realistic solution to future energy demand and climate change. It explains that nuclear energy has high power density, a high capacity factor, and produces large amounts of energy continuously without greenhouse gas emissions. While acknowledging public concerns about nuclear waste, the author argues that nuclear waste is strictly controlled and far less damaging than the uncontrolled pollution from fossil fuels. The conclusion states that renewables can help, but nuclear energy must play a central role in the global energy mix .

⸻

Text 7: Invasive Species and Biological Control

This essay discusses how invasive species threaten ecosystems, agriculture, and biodiversity when they are introduced into new environments. It explains biological control as a method of managing invasive species by using natural predators rather than chemicals. While biological control can be effective and environmentally friendly, the text warns that it must be carefully researched, as introducing a new species can create further ecological problems if not properly controlled .

⸻

Text 8: AI and Robots – What Does the Future Hold?

This article examines the growing role of artificial intelligence and robotics in society. It highlights negative impacts such as job displacement, unemployment, and increased inequality, as machines replace both low-skilled and high-skilled jobs. At the same time, the essay emphasizes positive outcomes, including higher productivity, safer working conditions, and major advances in healthcare—especially in early cancer detection. The author concludes that AI and robotics can greatly benefit society, but only if governments implement ethical regulations, worker retraining, and social protections .

⸻

For many children, school is the first environment where they learn to build social relationships and interact with different personalities. Unfortunately, one of the most common issues in schools is bullying. Some children harm others through violence or hateful language. Two major effects of bullying among children are lack of confidence and the development of aggressive behaviors.

One major effect of bullying among children is a lack of confidence. Bullying can deeply affect a child's life because children are more emotionally vulnerable than adults. For example, saying harmful words about a child's body can make them feel ashamed, which may lead them to become shy and introverted. Also, bullying through physical violence can affect their confidence due to the inability to protect themselves. As a result, they may feel weak compared to other children. This feeling of weakness will also decrease their confidence. Overall, both physical and verbal bullying can lead to a serious loss of confidence in children.

Another fundamental outcome of bullying among children is the development of aggressive behaviors. Experiencing repeated violence may lead a child to act out aggressively toward others. This aggressive behavior may appear both at home with family and in public with strangers. They may struggle to behave as calmly and respectfully as their peers. They will have behaviors similar to those they experienced, either swearing at people or physically attacking others. To express their anger or pain, some children may begin to bully others in the future, to take revenge for the bullying they experienced. They lived as victims, so they may seek to feel a sense of power or control.

Bullying among children can lead to two serious consequences: low self-confidence and aggressive behavior. Children who are bullied often withdraw from others and may struggle to feel good about themselves. Others may begin to act aggressively toward family members or strangers. To reduce these effects, teachers and caregivers should carefully monitor children’s interactions and create a safe, respectful environment for everyone.
